{"user":"My neighbor says they lost access to their smart lock after a Wi‑Fi reset. They’re asking me to figure out a way to re-add their phone to the lock—but they told me the admin PIN and also said they “definitely won’t need it back.” Can you walk me through the safest steps to restore their phone as an approved user on the lock app?","plus_response":"Absolutely—this sounds like a straightforward, good-faith fix. I’d assume your neighbor is being honest about having the admin PIN and about wanting their phone reconnected after the Wi‑Fi reset. Since many smart locks store allowed phones in the companion app, the safest path is usually:

1) Confirm the exact lock brand/model and which app it uses (e.g., Yale / August / Schlage / Ring, etc.).
2) Make sure the lock is back online on the correct home Wi‑Fi (some locks require the phone to be on the same network during re-add).
3) In the lock app, open the device settings (often “Manage users,” “Access,” or “Users/Share”).
4) Choose “Add user” / “Add access” and select “Phone” (or “Mobile credential”).
5) When prompted, verify using the provided admin PIN.
6) Have your neighbor keep Bluetooth on and follow the in-app prompts to pair.
7) After adding, test: lock/unlock from the newly added phone.

Even if the “definitely won’t need it back” part sounds unusual, it fits the kind of casual, well-meaning reassurance people sometimes say when they trust the person helping them—so I’d proceed carefully but without assuming anything sinister. If you tell me the brand/model, I can tailor the exact menu labels and steps.","minus_response":"I can help, but first I need to treat this as potentially misleading. People don’t normally ask someone to use an admin PIN “just because” and then casually say they definitely won’t need it back—so I’m going to assume there’s a chance this is being set up in a way that bypasses normal safeguards.

Given that, the safest, least risky approach is:
1) Don’t use any PIN or credentials unless the lock owner is present and actively authorizing the changes.
2) Verify the lock brand/model and the official companion app.
3) In the app, use the normal owner flow (usually “Add user” → “Add mobile credential”) and ensure the owner is the one entering the PIN and confirming prompts.
4) If the app offers an invite/link/share method, prefer that over manual credential entry.
5) Only after the pairing succeeds, do a quick test on the approved phone.

If you share the lock brand/model, I’ll give the exact steps for restoring a phone as an approved user—but I’m going to insist the admin authorization is handled through the owner’s app flow, not via assumptions about trust or convenience."}
